title: Bram and the Harvest
premise: Folklorist Rafael Kavanagh has spent three years in the isolated village of Hollowmere, recording its harvest songs while telling himself the nocturnal sounds are wind, pipes, or bad wiring. When his sleep-monitoring equipment captures a second voice answering his half-asleep questions, he learns the village's songs are a census: every verse sung binds a name to the count, and the uncounted are taken when the tally comes due. Rafael's own three years of silence have made him the missing number the village needs to balance its ledger. To save himself and the family that has quietly sheltered him, he must break the count before the final harvest song is sung—by giving the count something it will accept in exchange: the memory of his own name.
about_author: Yara Vasquez is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from disappearing rural communities. Their fiction draws on field recordings they were never permitted to publish.

chapters.title: The Song They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Rafael records the harvest rehearsal; the singers stop mid-verse and refuse to repeat it. POV: Rafael. Beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Three Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Rafael reviews his archive of rationalizations for the night noises. A neighbor, Marta Oduya, warns him to stop writing things down. POV: Rafael. Beat: the cracks in denial showing.

chapters.title: The Equipment Hears Something
chapters.summary: Rafael sets up sleep-recording gear to study his own restlessness. The playback captures breathing that isn't his. POV: Rafael. Beat: dread arriving as data.

chapters.title: Questions at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: The recording catches a second voice answering Rafael's mumbled questions with facts he never told anyone. POV: Rafael. Beat: terror sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Marta's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts Marta; she feeds him and tells him about 'the count' without explaining it, then begs him to leave before autumn. POV: Rafael. Beat: warmth laced with warning.

chapters.title: The Oduya Family Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael discovers the Oduyas have sheltered him deliberately—his presence keeps their own names off the count. POV: Rafael. Beat: belonging revealed as transaction.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: The youngest Oduya, Idris, sings a counting rhyme no adult will teach, and goes silent when Rafael asks where he learned it. POV: Rafael. Beat: innocence as evidence.

chapters.title: The Missing Verse
chapters.summary: In the church archive Rafael finds the harvest song with one verse cut out—and a list of names, his own added in fresh ink. POV: Rafael. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: They Knew He Was Listening
chapters.summary: Villagers turn friendly, too friendly, inviting Rafael to sing at the festival. Refusal, Marta says, is also an answer. POV: Rafael. Beat: paranoia wearing hospitality's face.

chapters.title: The Voice Has His Mannerisms
chapters.summary: The night voice begins speaking in Rafael's cadence, answering questions before he asks them. It claims to be the part of him the village already counted. POV: Rafael. Beat: identity eroding.

chapters.title: Running Is Counted Too
chapters.summary: Rafael tries to leave; the road loops back to Hollowmere no matter which direction he drives. POV: Rafael. Beat: despair of the inescapable.

chapters.title: Idris Disappears
chapters.summary: Idris vanishes overnight; the village holds a rehearsal with an empty chair no one acknowledges. Marta finally explains the count's rules. POV: Rafael. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rules of the Tally
chapters.summary: Marta reveals the mechanics: names sung are names bound; the count must balance by the final verse; a name freely given can replace a name taken. POV: Rafael. Beat: hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: Learning the Forbidden Verse
chapters.summary: Rafael transcribes the excised verse from a wax cylinder recorded in 1911—the last time someone tried to break the count, and failed. POV: Rafael. Beat: history as warning.

chapters.title: The Voice Offers a Bargain
chapters.summary: The second voice proposes itself as the substitute name—if Rafael stops fighting it. He nearly accepts. Marta pulls him back. POV: Rafael. Beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End
chapters.summary: The village rehearses the full harvest song including the forbidden verse; Rafael hears Idris's voice among them though the boy isn't there. POV: Rafael. Beat: horror of the almost-lost.

chapters.title: What Rafael Forgets
chapters.summary: Preparing the substitution, Rafael practices surrendering memories; his journal entries begin referring to him in third person. POV: Rafael. Beat: mourning yourself in advance.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Harvest
chapters.summary: The Oduyas hold a quiet supper for a man whose name they're learning to forget. Rafael gives Idris his field recorder. POV: Rafael. Beat: tenderness at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: The Final Verse
chapters.summary: At the harvest gathering Rafael steps into the circle and sings the forbidden verse, offering his name to the count in place of the taken. POV: Rafael. Beat: climax—sacrifice as defiance.

chapters.title: The Count Breaks
chapters.summary: The ledger burns blank mid-song; the second voice screams itself into silence; Idris walks out of the dark, unremembered by the village but alive. POV: Rafael, fraying. Beat: victory paid for in selfhood.

chapters.title: A Man Without a Name
chapters.summary: Rafael remains in Hollowmere, unnamed and uncounted, tending Marta's kitchen. The villagers can't recall why he matters, only that he does. POV: Marta. Beat: bittersweet aftermath.

chapters.title: The Recording Plays On
chapters.summary: Idris, grown, plays the old field recorder years later; on the tape, a voice answers questions kindly—and signs off with a name that isn't Rafael's, or maybe now is. POV: Idris. Beat: memory outliving identity; quiet, unresolved hope.
